html:
SMTO-SKL-0076 — Your Microsoft account isn't allowed to do this

GUID: 128f3482-57dc-5b2d-a917-a908b73e3ec0
Slug: microsoft365-graph-forbidden
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • Microsoft says the account connected to SMTO doesn't have permission for this email, calendar, contact or file. Microsoft refused the request, so nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Sign in to Outlook, OneDrive or SharePoint in your browser with the same Microsoft account and try to open or change the item yourself. SMTO can only do what this account is allowed to do.
  2. If the item belongs to someone else, such as a shared mailbox, calendar or file, ask its owner to give your account edit access. Viewing access alone doesn't let SMTO make changes for you.
  3. Ask SMTO to connect your Microsoft 365 account again for this kind of task, for example “connect my Microsoft account to send mail”, and approve Microsoft's page. If an administrator removed or limited SMTO's access, connecting again asks Microsoft for it afresh.
  4. If Microsoft's page says an administrator must approve, ask your organization's IT team to approve SMTO's Microsoft app. Some organizations block these permissions until an administrator allows them.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the request without a permission message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to your organization's Microsoft 365 administrator or the person who manages SMTO. Don't connect a different person's Microsoft account to get around the permission.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft Graph returned 403 Forbidden (or provider code ErrorAccessDenied): the signed-in delegated user, the granted scopes, or tenant policy does not permit this operation on the target resource.

What this means

  • Graph returns HTTP 403 or the provider code ErrorAccessDenied. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Graph returns HTTP 403 or the provider code ErrorAccessDenied.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect delegated feature scopes and resource/user permissions separately; denial does not prove expired credentials.

How to fix it

  • Compare the account's authorized_features (microsoft365.connection_status) with the operation's required feature and check the signed-in user's own rights on the target resource (shared mailbox, delegated calendar, another user's file). If a feature is missing, call microsoft365.connect again with the same app and account_key and only the needed feature; tenant policy may require administrator consent in Microsoft Entra.
  • Check the signed-in user's access and exact granted feature scopes. Request consent only for the needed feature.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended account meets the actual access requirement for that resource.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
